say: This van driver just beeped Gary for stopping. Ten seconds later, he nearly ran someone *over.*
High street. Gary's turning *left* into a side road. Indicator on.
At the corner, Margaret's *waiting* to cross the side road. So Gary stops, and lets her go.
Behind him, Wayne. White van. Late for a job. And he leans on the *horn.*
Window down. Move! She hasn't even started crossing! *You've* got priority!
So Wayne swings out, *round* Gary, and turns into the side road.
Straight at Margaret. He slams on the brakes, *inches* from her.
And all of it is on Gary's *dashcam.*
Since twenty twenty two, rule H two says, at a junction, you should give way to pedestrians *crossing,* or *waiting* to cross, the road you're turning into.
Waiting *counts.* Margaret didn't have to be in the road yet. Gary was right to stop.
Wayne? Rule one six seven. Don't *overtake* at a junction. Rule one one two. You must not use your horn while *stationary,* and never aggressively.
Gary sends the clip to the police. Dashcam footage can be used as *evidence.*
Nearly hitting a pedestrian like that can be *careless* *driving.* A hundred pound fine and three points, or up to *nine* in court.
Wayne, *guilty.* Did you know waiting counts? Follow for case six.
